To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we identified FGFR3-TAC3 fusion proteins as drivers of resistance to EGFR/ERBB3 blockade in an HNSCC xenotransplant model.

we identified FGFR3-Tacc3 fusion proteins as naturally occurring drivers that substitute for EGFR signaling in EGFR-dependent tumors, and that this resistance pathway is specific to tumors with active EGFR signaling.
FGFR3 TACC3 fusion proteins are naturally occurring drivers of acquired resistance to EGFR inhibition.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the discovery of mechanisms of acquired resistance in HNSCC and other EGFR-dependent cancers, which is of great clinical significance as these cancers are currently treated with EGFR-blocking therapies.
the discovery of novel mechanisms of acquired resistance to targeted therapy, which is of critical importance for the development of novel therapeutic strategies to improve patient outcomes.
the development of novel therapies for cancer.

the FGFR3-TAC3 fusion proteins act in a similar fashion as EGFR in the context of EGFR-dependent cancer, but are not able to act in a similar manner in the context of PIK3CA-dependent cancers.
FGFR3 TACC3 fusions promote resistance to EGFR blockade in HNSCC by functionally substitututing for EGFR and ERK signaling, rather than ERBB2/PI3K signaling.
FGFR3/TACC3 fusions are capable to substitute EGFR signaling in HNSCC.

we have discovered a novel mechanism of resistance to EGFR inhibition in head and neck cancer.
